description: Dedicated reference entries for the stages and pressures of Kaysender's invention workflow.

entries.title: Invention Conceptualization
entries.summary: Inventors begin by defining a concrete goal and identifying whether the work is a magical item, device, ship part, spell, or enchantment.
body: Conceptualization establishes what an invention is intended to accomplish before resources are spent. The chosen category identifies the knowledge, tools, and specialists most relevant to the project.

Magical items emphasize arcane understanding; mechanical and clockwork devices draw on tinkering; ship parts may require engineering, navigation, or smithing; spells rely on arcane research; and vessel enchantments can combine magic with practical trades.

entries.title: Invention Research and Development
entries.summary: Research tests whether an inventor has found a viable path before committing fully to construction.
body: Research may involve consulting experts, comparing prior designs, experimenting with ideas, and identifying the materials or methods that can make the concept work.
A clear breakthrough improves later work, partial understanding demands more testing, and failure suggests changing materials, methods, or sources of expertise before proceeding.

sections.heading: Legacy Research Procedure
body: The source provides tiered DC results and modifiers to the next crafting check. These numerical procedures require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Invention System / Research and Development Phase

entries.title: Invention Materials and Preparation
entries.summary: Required materials should follow from the invention's purpose and may demand acquisition, refinement, or substitution.
body: Material gathering is part of the invention rather than a detached shopping step. Components should reflect what the device, spell, enchantment, or ship part is meant to do.

Scarcity, poor quality, and delayed acquisition can reshape the project. Inventors may need expeditions, suppliers, specialist preparation, or a revised design when the ideal material cannot be obtained.

sections.heading: Legacy Gathering Procedure
body: The source provides tiered gathering checks and modifiers to later crafting. These numerical procedures require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Invention System / Materials Gathering and Preparation

entries.title: Invention Crafting and Enchanting
entries.summary: The central construction stage can produce a flawed device, a working design, an exceptional result, or a catastrophic loss.
body: Once materials and a viable approach are ready, the inventor assembles, fabricates, or enchants the project. Success is not purely binary: a creation may function imperfectly, meet its goal, or reveal capabilities beyond the original plan.
Failure may waste components or leave a defective prototype. Severe failure can destroy the work, damage the workshop, or injure those nearby.

sections.heading: Legacy Construction Procedure
body: The source provides several DC bands, subsequent-check modifiers, and catastrophic outcomes. These numerical procedures require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Invention System / Crafting or Enchanting Phase

entries.title: Invention Testing
entries.summary: Completed inventions must be operated, cast, or installed to expose hidden benefits and dangerous flaws.
body: Testing places the invention in the conditions where it is meant to function. A device is operated, a spell is cast, or a ship component is installed so its actual behavior can be compared with its design.
Minor defects can guide adjustment, while excellent testing may reveal an unexpected benefit. Serious malfunction can ruin materials, harm operators, or prove the design must be scrapped.

sections.heading: Legacy Testing Procedure
body: The source provides tiered testing results and modifiers to improvement attempts. These numerical procedures require conversion.

entries.title: Invention Improvement
entries.summary: Working inventions can undergo further research and modification, but improvement may also damage a successful design.
body: Improvement begins after an initial version exists. Inventors can refine function through additional study, testing, replacement parts, or enchantment.
Successful iteration ranges from negligible refinement to near-perfect performance. Failed changes may reduce effectiveness, make the invention hazardous, or destroy the value of earlier work.

sections.heading: Legacy Improvement Procedure
body: The source provides tiered improvement checks and functionality modifiers. These numerical procedures require conversion.

entries.title: Invention Success Factors and Failure Costs
entries.summary: Material quality, expertise, assistance, funding, time, and magic improve projects, while repeated failure compounds waste and danger.
body: Rare materials, knowledgeable assistance, magical tools, specialist expertise, adequate funding, and preparation time can all strengthen an invention attempt. These advantages represent better conditions rather than substitutes for a coherent design.

Failure consumes materials and time. Major failure can force a rebuild, critical failure may cause injury or explosion, and repeated failure encourages inventors to change their approach or obtain outside help.

sections.heading: Legacy Modifiers and Fallout
body: The source assigns numerical bonuses, penalties, and failure thresholds. These procedures require conversion.
